author: k. j. simms
title: Springbrook Center ranks 3rd in size among Cumberland County nursing homes in Q1 2026
text:
Springbrook Center was the third-largest nursing facility in Cumberland County during the first quarter of 2026, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) reported .
The nursing center provided 123 beds, which is 34 more than the county’s average as of early 2026. Springbrook Center was home to an average of 112.1 residents during this period.
CMS gave Springbrook Center an overall rating of 2 out of 5, below the 2.9 average rating for Maine nursing homes.
Barron Center led the county in size during the quarter, offering 219 beds, while Seaside Nursing and Retirement Home followed with 147 beds available.
By the end of the first quarter of 2026, Springbrook Center had been subject to two fines totaling $17,388 and incurred three penalties.
Cumberland County, Maine, had 11 for-profit nursing homes in total.
U.S. Census Bureau estimates indicate that the U.S. older adult population is increasing, even as the population of younger residents declines. From 2020 to 2024, the number of Americans age 65 and older grew by 13%, while those under 18 decreased by 1.7%. The older adult population has surged from 4.9 million in 1920 to over 61 million in 2024.
Research from 2021 suggests that approximately half of Americans in this group—roughly 28 million—may eventually need long-term services and support. The same study anticipates more than a third could require nursing home care at some point.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome , executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
